questions.prompt: You need to teach a seven-tier rank table with XP thresholds people will look up repeatedly. Which section kind?
questions.explanation: Slides. Reference material has to stay scannable and re-findable — a learner coming back for one threshold can page to it. A video buries the same table in a timeline nobody wants to scrub through.

answers.text: SLIDES — reference material stays scannable and easy to return to
VIDEO — narration makes the tiers memorable
QUIZ — testing the thresholds teaches them
WALKTHROUGH — point at the rank badge in the app

questions.prompt: Why can't you author walkthrough steps in the course editor?
questions.explanation: Steps target UI elements by anchor id, so they must live beside the code that provides those anchors. In the repo, a rename fails the build and names the broken step; in the database, the same rename breaks a live tour with nothing in the diff to catch it.

answers.text: Steps live in repo files so a UI rename fails the build instead of silently breaking a tour
The editor can't render the tour overlay
Only admins are allowed to create walkthroughs
Steps are generated automatically from the anchor registry

questions.prompt: What should every quiz question carry besides its options?
questions.explanation: An explanation, shown after grading. A question that only says "wrong" filters people; a question that explains why gets a second attempt at teaching the thing they just demonstrated they didn't know.

answers.text: An explanation shown after grading
A difficulty rating
A time limit
A link to the section it came from

questions.prompt: What is the AI course generator good for, and what is it not? Select the true statements.
questions.explanation: It's genuinely good at proposing structure and drafting bodies you then edit. It cannot write walkthrough steps — it has no knowledge of the anchor registry or what's on screen — and it will state things about Constellation confidently and wrongly, because it writes from your prompt rather than from the code.

answers.text: Good for proposing an outline and drafting section bodies
Cannot write walkthrough steps
Its factual claims about Constellation can be trusted without checking
It assigns the finished course to the right members automatically

questions.prompt: You're setting up a module and wondering whether to make it sequential. What's the default, and why?
questions.explanation: Sequential. Teaching has an order — later sections assume earlier ones. If the order genuinely doesn't matter, that's a signal you've written a reference document rather than a course, and it may belong somewhere other than the course system.

answers.text: Sequential — and if order truly doesn't matter, you may have written a reference doc, not a course
Any order — learners should pick what interests them
Sequential only for modules containing a quiz
It makes no difference; gating is set per section
